source.title: Research Report: Alternative sparsity methods for sparse autoencoders with OthelloGPT.

record.file_problem: none; the full post, including the appendix and comments, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study varies SAE sparsity-training methods and reports unexplained reconstruction variance, which bears on whether SAE error depends on the training method. It does not use the original dark-matter analysis.
record.gate_note: The study reports reconstruction-error measurements for several SAE training variants, relevant to V6. Its good-classifier counts, sparsity percentages, and dead-neuron results do not measure the dark-matter claims and are not recorded as rows. The text gives no L1 or no-sparsity reconstruction-error value for comparison.
record.test_reason: The post compares alternative SAE sparsity methods on OthelloGPT by how many good board-position classifiers they yield. Unexplained variance is reported only as a side metric for SAEs picked by classifier count. It gives no L1 or no-sparsity variance value and does not analyze the error's structure, predictability, scaling or functional role. The post predates the original source and does not address the dark-matter claim. Its reconstruction numbers cannot show whether error shrinks with better training (V6), so it does not test any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The author finds smoothed-L0, leaky top-k and dimension-reduction methods gave more good classifiers than L1 (45 for leaky top-k vs 29 for L1). He calls the search heuristic and not strong evidence to replace L1. No conclusion about SAE error structure is drawn.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares alternative SAE sparsity losses and activation functions on OthelloGPT, rather than applying the original dark-matter analysis.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported unexplained variance differs across sparsity methods and selected hyperparameter settings; values are for selected best SAEs from a heuristic search, not a controlled matched comparison.

fits_no_version.finding: Across sparsity methods, the best-classifier SAEs on OthelloGPT layer 3 have 7.7–18.5% unexplained variance at differing sparsities. Leaky top-k with ε>0 (no dead neurons) and ε=0 (15.1% dead) both give 13.2%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE reconstruction error on OthelloGPT varies with the sparsity method, but no L1 baseline or matched sparsity is given; dead latents did not change unexplained variance in leaky top-k.

record.problems: The author says the hyperparameter search was heuristic and not exhaustive. The reported error values are for selected best SAEs, with no L1 or no-sparsity reconstruction-error baseline stated and no uncertainty estimates. The study uses a single OthelloGPT setting and does not analyze the residual's structure.
record.rows_left_out: Good-classifier counts, sparsity percentages, and dead-neuron measurements are omitted because they do not measure the dark-matter claims. Values represented only in the result plots are not extracted because the text gives no numerical values for them.

untested.parts: Linear predictability of SAE error from input activations
Error-norm predictability across SAE sizes, same-context failures, persistence with scale
Loss impact of spliced reconstructions versus random errors of the same size
Split of error into unlearned features versus nonlinear error
Loss of circuit or steering behaviour without the error term
Whether error shrinks with better architectures or training objectives against a matched L1 baseline; no residual-structure analysis

record.verdict_notes: The record's 'tests/T2' for V6 is not supported: the unexplained-variance values are side metrics of SAEs chosen by classifier count, with no L1 value reported. The relation 'discusses' is the closest enum value; the post is really T6 and only tangentially relevant.

versions.untested_parts: Whether a large share of SAE error is linearly predictable from input activations.
Error-norm predictability across SAE sizes, same-context failures across sizes, and whether error persists with scale.
Whether SAE reconstruction replacement harms model loss more than same-size random errors.
Whether predictable error contains unlearned features and nonlinear error resists further dictionary learning.
Whether omitting SAE error causes meaningful losses in circuits, steering, or other model behavior.

The study varies sparsity-training methods and measures reconstruction variance, but does not establish whether dark matter mostly reflects training artifacts, compare residuals against a reported L1 or no-sparsity baseline, test end-to-end training, or analyze residual structure.
